Name: Kowloon Soy Company
Location: G/F, 9 Graham Street, Central, Hong Kong, Hong Kong SAR, China
Description: Traditional soy sauce and condiment shop founded in 1917, now the remaining retail outlet of Kowloon Soy Co. Sells soy sauces, pickles and fermented tofu in the Graham Street market lane. Why: A century-old Hong Kong soy maker whose top-tier sauce is fermented in clay jars and sold locally; easy pantry souvenir, with plastic bottles available for flights.

Name: G.O.D. (Goods of Desire), Hollywood Road
Location: 48 Hollywood Road, Central, Hong Kong, Hong Kong SAR, China
Description: Flagship-area store of Hong Kong lifestyle brand G.O.D., selling homewares, apparel and gifts with a nostalgic Hong Kong-slang humour. Why: Hong Kong design label (founded by Douglas Young) that repackages local nostalgia: tong lau, mahjong, bing sutt themes.

Name: PMQ (Police Married Quarters)
Location: 35 Aberdeen Street, Central, Hong Kong, Hong Kong SAR, China
Description: Former police married quarters turned creative hub with designer studios, shops, cafes and courtyard events. Why: The main place to meet Hong Kong independent designers and makers in one building; has run Christmas bazaars and displays in past years.

Name: Ladies' Market (Tung Choi Street)
Location: Tung Choi Street, Mong Kok, Hong Kong, Hong Kong SAR, China
Description: Long street of stalls selling clothes, accessories, souvenirs and phone cases; bargaining is the norm. Why: Hong Kong's best-known bargain street market, in the middle of the Mong Kok market cluster.

Name: Temple Street Night Market
Location: Temple Street, between Jordan Road and Kansu Street, Yau Ma Tei, Hong Kong, Hong Kong SAR, China
Description: Evening street market of stalls selling souvenirs, menswear, electronics and trinkets, with food stalls and fortune tellers nearby. Why: Classic Hong Kong night-market atmosphere; the street is a part-time pedestrian zone and popular with photographers after dark.

Name: Upper Lascar Row (Cat Street)
Location: Upper Lascar Row, Sheung Wan, Hong Kong, Hong Kong SAR, China
Description: Pedestrian lane of small family-run stalls and shops selling ceramics, jade, Cultural Revolution memorabilia and vintage Hong Kong collectibles. Why: Cheaper, more casual cousin of Hollywood Road's antique dealers; good for browsing even if buying nothing.

Name: Sham Shui Po fabric, leather and paper streets
Location: Ki Lung, Nam Cheong, Tai Nan, Kiu Kiang and Shek Kip Mei Streets, Sham Shui Po, Hong Kong, Hong Kong SAR, China
Description: Grid of wholesale-style shops for fabric, buttons, lace, leather and paper. The old Yen Chow Street fabric bazaar moved in 2023 to a market on Tung Chau Street. Why: Hong Kong's craft and haberdashery heartland; shops like Wa Fat Piece Goods (1J Shek Kip Mei St), Luen Hing Paper (168 Kiu Kiang St) and Brothers Leathercraft (207-209 Tai Nan St) serve designers and hobbyists.

Name: Apliu Street flea market
Location: Apliu Street, Sham Shui Po (MTR exit A2/C2), Hong Kong, Hong Kong SAR, China
Description: Street of hawker stalls and small shops selling electronics, phone parts, hi-fi, camera gear and odd secondhand items. Why: Hong Kong's electronics bazaar; Ying Kee Trading at 154 Apliu St sells photo accessories.

Name: Good Bad Creative
Location: Shop B1, 124 Nam Cheong Street, Sham Shui Po, Kowloon, Hong Kong, Hong Kong SAR, China
Description: Secondhand shop full of 1980s-90s toys, cassettes and magazines. Why: Good for Hong Kong pop-culture nostalgia in Sham Shui Po's indie-shop cluster.

Name: Hak Dei
Location: G/F, 618 Shanghai Street, Mong Kok, Kowloon, Hong Kong, Hong Kong SAR, China
Description: Retro-minded shop stocking local ceramics, bamboo steamers and kitchen gadgets. Why: A convenient place to pick up Hong Kong-style bamboo steamers and kitchen pieces in one stop.

Name: Dongpohk
Location: 17 Shing Wong Street, Sheung Wan, Hong Kong, Hong Kong SAR, China
Description: Neighbourhood shop in a historic tenement selling local snacks, toys and vintage pieces. Why: Tong lau-set shop that mixes everyday Hong Kong goods with vintage finds.

Name: JikSap
Location: 9/F, Block A, On Lok Factory Building, 90 Kowloon City Road, To Kwa Wan, Kowloon, Hong Kong, Hong Kong SAR, China
Description: Large vintage store in an industrial building selling prints, toys and furniture. Why: Pairs well with a 13 Streets walk in To Kwa Wan.

Name: Muze Pens
Location: G/F, 236 Tai Nan Street, Sham Shui Po, Kowloon, Hong Kong, Hong Kong SAR, China
Description: Fine pens, inks and premium paper, with products available to try. Why: Sits comfortably in Sham Shui Po's paper and craft area for stationery fans.

Name: Kobo Camera
Location: Room 706, 7/F, Witty Commercial Building, 1A-1L Tung Choi Street, Mong Kok, Kowloon, Hong Kong, Hong Kong SAR, China
Description: Small shop near the Ladies' Market selling new film cameras and a curated vintage selection, with staff happy to help beginners. Why: A friendly entry point to Hong Kong's film camera scene.

Name: Sunrise Photo Co
Location: Shop B2, 333 Lai Chi Kok Road, Sham Shui Po, Kowloon, Hong Kong, Hong Kong SAR, China
Description: Photo shop established in 1973 offering printing and a large secondhand film camera and lens selection; also buys used cameras. Has a cat mascot. Why: Old-school Sham Shui Po camera dealer; combine with Apliu Street.

Name: Dried seafood street (Des Voeux Road West)
Location: Des Voeux Road West between Queen Street and Main Street, plus Wing Lok Street and Bonham Strand West, Hong Kong, Hong Kong SAR, China
Description: Trade street of baskets of dried abalone, scallops, sea cucumber, fish maw and dried mushrooms; Wing Lok Street leans to ginseng and bird's nest. Why: Last visible stretch of Hong Kong's historic dried-seafood trade; vivid and photogenic.

Name: Tuck Chong Sum Kee Bamboo Steamer Company
Location: G/F, 12 Western Street, Sai Ying Pun, Hong Kong, Hong Kong SAR, China
Description: One of the few Hong Kong shops still making bamboo steamers by hand, run by a fifth-generation owner and long a supplier to teahouses. Also sells bamboo household items. Why: A genuine last-of-their-trade craft shop; a handmade steamer is a distinctive Hong Kong kitchen souvenir.

Name: Goldfish Market (Tung Choi Street North)
Location: Tung Choi Street North, Mong Kok, Hong Kong, Hong Kong SAR, China
Description: Roughly 300 m stretch of shops selling goldfish, aquarium gear and other pets, hung with bags of fish. Why: Goldfish are a lucky symbol, and the street is a striking, only-in-Hong-Kong sight.

Name: Flower Market Road
Location: Flower Market Road, Prince Edward, Hong Kong, Hong Kong SAR, China
Description: Long avenue of florists and plant sellers spilling blooms onto the pavement. Why: Colourful and photogenic, and festive plants may be on display in late December.

Name: Sneakers Street (Fa Yuen Street)
Location: Fa Yuen Street, Mong Kok, Hong Kong, Hong Kong SAR, China
Description: Street lined with sportswear and sneaker shops, from major brands to limited editions. Why: Hong Kong's best-known sneaker shopping strip; holiday sales are common.

Name: Fook Ming Tong Tea Shop (IFC Mall)
Location: 3/F, IFC Mall, 8 Finance Street, Central (unit listed as 3006 or 3015), Hong Kong, Hong Kong SAR, China
Description: Branch of the Hong Kong tea chain founded in 1987 that sells loose tea and teaware, with tasting. Also has outlets at Harbour City, a Causeway Bay SOGO counter and the airport. Why: A Hong Kong-founded tea brand with knowledgeable staff and tastings; easy tea souvenir.

Name: K11 MUSEA
Location: 18 Salisbury Road, Tsim Sha Tsui, Hong Kong, Hong Kong SAR, China
Description: Art-led luxury mall on the Tsim Sha Tsui waterfront with direct access to the Avenue of Stars and Salisbury Garden. Why: The most design-driven mall in Kowloon; seasonal programmes and harbour-facing installations have appeared in past Decembers.

Name: Harbour City
Location: Canton Road and Ocean Terminal Forecourt, Tsim Sha Tsui, Hong Kong, Hong Kong SAR, China
Description: Hong Kong's largest shopping complex, with a free open-air Ocean Terminal Forecourt Christmas display in recent years. Why: The 2025 season ran 12 Nov 2025 - 4 Jan 2026 with a Disney-themed 9 m centrepiece and evening snow effects, so a similar display is likely for Christmas 2026.

Name: Kai Tak Mall (Kai Tak Sports Park)
Location: Kai Tak Sports Park, Kai Tak, Hong Kong, Hong Kong SAR, China
Description: Roughly 700,000 sq ft, three-building mall at the sports park (opened 2025) with around 200 stores, sports brands, a Liverpool FC flagship and about 80 restaurants. Why: New sports-led mall that drew a record New Year's Eve crowd, and a gateway to the Kai Tak waterfront.

Name: Linva Tailor
Location: 38 Cochrane Street, Central, Hong Kong, Hong Kong SAR, China
Description: Traditional cheongsam tailor opened in 1965; custom garments are made by hand. Why: One of the last Shanghainese-style cheongsam makers, with few apprentices.

Name: Choi Kee birdcage workshop (Yuen Po Street Bird Garden)
Location: Yuen Po Street Bird Garden, Prince Edward, Hong Kong, Hong Kong SAR, China
Description: Stall of Chan Lok-choi, described as possibly Hong Kong's last birdcage maker, who mostly repairs cages now. The garden itself is listed as open 07:00-20:00 daily. Why: A living last-of-trade craft inside a bird market that is good for photography.

Name: Chinese Arts & Crafts, Pacific Place
Location: Shop 320, The Mall, Pacific Place, 88 Queensway, Admiralty, Hong Kong, Hong Kong SAR, China
Description: Department-store-style shop for Chinese silks, porcelain, jade, embroidery and gifts. Why: Long-standing source of Chinese crafts, though reviews say the range has changed.

Name: Man Wa Lane chop stalls
Location: Man Wa Lane, Sheung Wan (short lane between Des Voeux Road Central and Wing Lok Street, near Sheung Wan MTR), Hong Kong, Hong Kong SAR, China
Description: A tiny alley of seal-carving (chop) stalls where craftsmen cut a personalised Chinese-character stamp from stone, wood, jade or even buffalo horn. Tell them your name and they suggest an auspicious Chinese rendering, then carve it while you wait or on a later visit. Why: One of the last places in Hong Kong where seal-carving is still practised by hand; a carved name chop is a distinctive, low-cost souvenir. A 2025 SCMP roundup noted more than a dozen stalls survive but few owners still carve by hand.

Name: Lee Kung Man Knitting
Location: Shop 2, G/F, 188 Nam Cheong Street, Sham Shui Po, Kowloon, Hong Kong, Hong Kong SAR, China
Description: Hong Kong's oldest underwear and knitwear maker (founded 1923), best known for its Golden Deer cotton vests and singlets, plus Blue Deer, Kwong Wah and Autumn Cicada ranges. The shop sells the classic ribbed vests and has done fashion collaborations in recent years. Why: A century-old local label whose deer-brand vests are a staple of 'old Hong Kong' fashion, with Sham Shui Po's fabric and haberdashery streets next door.

Name: Chan Chi Kee Cutlery
Location: 316-318 Shanghai Street, Yau Ma Tei, Kowloon, Hong Kong, Hong Kong SAR, China
Description: A family-run knife and kitchen-tool shop on the Shanghai Street kitchenware strip, famous for Chinese cleavers and slicing knives (stainless and carbon steel), plus woks, ladles, meat hooks and bamboo tools. Staff are said to speak English and advise on knife choice. Why: One of the oldest knife makers in the city (family says prewar; one source says the 1920s) and supplier to hotels and restaurants worldwide; Anthony Bourdain bought a cleaver here.

Name: Shanghai Street kitchenware strip
Location: Shanghai Street, between Jordan Road and Argyle Street, Yau Ma Tei / Mong Kok, Kowloon, Hong Kong, Hong Kong SAR, China
Description: A long stretch of shops selling restaurant-grade kitchenware: woks, cleavers, bamboo steamers, clay pots, enamelware and plastic gear, alongside wedding shops and the odd old dai pai dong. Chan Chi Kee is the best-known knife shop. Why: Hong Kong's traditional 'kitchen street': restaurant-trade pricing and tools you won't find in malls, in a cluster of tong lau shopfronts.

Name: Jade Market (Yau Ma Tei)
Location: Kansu Street and Battery Street, under the flyover, Yau Ma Tei, Kowloon, Hong Kong, Hong Kong SAR, China
Description: A covered market of roughly 400-odd small stalls selling jade pendants, bangles and beads, pearls and trinkets. It is next to the Temple Street night market area and a short walk from Yau Ma Tei MTR Exit C. Why: A long-running street market for jade where locals haggle over lucky charms; the browsing, not necessarily buying, is the draw, with graded versus dyed jade a minefield for novices.

Name: Yue Hwa Chinese Products Emporium
Location: 301-309 Nathan Road, Yau Ma Tei (Jordan), Kowloon, Hong Kong, Hong Kong SAR, China
Description: A multi-floor department store of Chinese goods: tea, herbs and medicine, silk, jade and porcelain, ceramics, calligraphy supplies, clothes, gifts and snacks. Why: The classic mainland-products emporium, founded in Hong Kong in 1959; a one-stop shop for tea, Chinese medicine and souvenirs, often cheaper than tourist stalls.

Name: Wing On Department Store (Sheung Wan)
Location: Wing On Centre, 211 Des Voeux Road Central, Sheung Wan, Hong Kong, Hong Kong SAR, China
Description: The flagship of the historic Wing On department-store chain (founded 1907), selling fashion, homeware and Chinese-style products; it traces back to the original Wing On building on Des Voeux Road Central. Why: Wing On and Sincere were Hong Kong's first Chinese-owned department stores and symbols of the 20th-century commercial class; this is the surviving link to that era in Sheung Wan.

Name: Ying Kee Tea House
Location: 151 Queen's Road Central, Central, Hong Kong (one of nine HK branches incl. Wan Chai, Causeway Bay, TST, Mong Kok), Hong Kong SAR, China
Description: A long-established Hong Kong tea merchant selling Chinese teas by weight (pu'er, oolong, jasmine, tieguanyin), tea gift sets and ware, and tea-based snacks and drinks. Its pastel-green storefronts mark nine branches. Why: One of the best-known local tea brands, a good place to buy gift teas at fair prices; Ying Kee even runs a bubble-tea spinoff.

Name: Kubrick and Broadway Cinematheque
Location: Shop H2, G/F, Prosperous Garden, 3 Public Square Street, Yau Ma Tei, Kowloon, Hong Kong, Hong Kong SAR, China
Description: Hong Kong's arthouse-cinema hub: Broadway Cinematheque screens indie films, festivals and director retrospectives, while the attached Kubrick bookshop-café sells film books, DVDs, soundtracks, posters and design goods with seating for coffee. Why: A film-lover's anchor in Yau Ma Tei and one of the only arthouse cinemas in the city, tucked inside a public housing estate's lower floor.

Name: Established Hong Kong tailors (Sam's Tailor, W.W. Chan, Ascot Chang)
Location: Sam's Tailor: Burlington Arcade, 90-94C Nathan Road, Tsim Sha Tsui; W.W. Chan & Sons: Unit B, 8/F Entertainment Building, 30 Queen's Road Central; Ascot Chang: several shops (one guide lists Elements, Tsim Sha Tsui), Hong Kong, Hong Kong SAR, China
Description: Three of the best-known names in Hong Kong bespoke: Sam's Tailor (a Nathan Road institution that has dressed celebrities and politicians), W.W. Chan & Sons (a long-established house on Queen's Road Central) and Ascot Chang (made-to-measure shirts and suits). Why: Tailoring is a Hong Kong specialty; the established houses are slower and more expensive than quick-turn shops but far more reliable.
